summary: A Quote client gets a full tick with its trade time, then a tick with only a new price: Firstock's V2 ticks are deltas merged over the snapshot, and the new price comes without a trade time, so the Quote frame has no old trade's time (it falls back to the receipt time); the next tick with a price and its time carries that time again.

notes: Audit R107-10 (codex/WEBSOCKET_PARITY_REVIEW_1.0.7.md): the old trade time inherited by a new price. The time-bearing tick is ltp_then_quote's full packet.

deviations.reason: Firstock's i_last_trade_time is in epoch seconds and the web sends it unchanged as ltt; feed timestamps are epoch milliseconds (docs/prompt/websockets-format.md). On a tick with a new price and no trade time the web sends the previous trade's time from its snapshot: a trade time goes with the price it came with and never carries over to a new one (lead rule, .lane/107/decisions.md and review-fixes.md: a per-packet time never carries over; audit R107-10). The desktop sends the trade time in ms, and for the price without its time the time it made the tick, as for any packet without one.
deviations.ref: firstock_adapter.py:828-870 ("ltt": data.get("i_last_trade_time", 0)); firstock_websocket.py::_on_message (merges each tick into the snapshot)

deviations.reason: The web's Quote sends oi 0 for an equity whose tick carries no open interest (data.get("i_open_interest", 0)); a value the broker did not send is left out, never sent as 0 (docs/api/websocket-streaming/quote.md, web openalgo#2376). The desktop's Quote leaves it out.
